notes: WebKit does not run in this container. The tester's run of the five remaining projects (webkit, webkit-iphone, firefox, firefox-download-navigation, chromium-plain-http) ended 57 failed, 51 passed, 2 skipped: every failure is browserType.launch - 'Host system is missing dependencies' naming libgtk-4.so.1, libgstreamer-1.0.so.0, libflite.so.1 and more - and all 57 are in the webkit and webkit-iphone projects. The 51 passed and 2 skipped are the firefox, firefox-download-navigation and chromium-plain-http rows, and they are exactly the implementer's reported 51 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed for that leg. So the implementer's trickyParts sentence that webkit's 'downloaded browsers launch and their projects ran green here' is not carried by its own totals: the 57 webkit rows are not in them. Nothing of the change turns on it - the webkit and webkit-iphone projects are green at the code head in CI's dispatch job, which runs every project - and it is recorded here so the reviewer reads that sentence with the numbers beside it rather than as evidence.

The pod's browser harness killed a sibling role's Postgres while this phase started, and the durable fix is this issue's retro output. At 03:27 UTC, `bash /legion/harness/setup.sh` in the tester's container started a second postmaster because its guard is `pg_ctl -D ... status`, which reads postmaster.pid and finds another container's PID absent from this PID namespace; the second postmaster refused the port, shut down, and removed the live server's lock file, and the live server did an immediate shutdown a minute later (/legion/harness/log/postgres.log, 03:27:32 and 03:28:36). The tester restarted the cluster and every run recorded here ran on it. The finding went to the INFRA controller on Envoy with its evidence, as the architect directed; the controller decided it is this tree's retro learning rather than an issue of its own, landing in docs/solutions/testing/a-browser-harness-in-an-issue-pod-lives-on-the-issue-volume-INFRA-43.md (guard the start on `pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1 -p $PG_PORT -q`, with the PID-namespace reason) and in the port-holder document's section 2. The implementer has already changed this pod's own copy of setup.sh; nothing in the repository has changed. It is not a defect of the change under test and did not affect a result.

What the fix does not cover, recorded so the reviewer is not surprised: the row now places the turn itself, so it no longer sees the reader-visible defect that produced the flake - the Conversation leaving a phone reader at the top of the page with the newest turn behind the composer, filed as dispatch://INFRA-303. The row keeps an assertion that names that state if its own probe point ever lands under the composer again (phone.e2e.ts:639-642), so the row is independent of INFRA-303 rather than blind to it at its own point. The Inbox leg's two checks (onWord, onFirstLowerEdge) are still one-shot document.elementFromPoint reads with no settle; they passed 30 of 30 at the head, 120 of 120 under the tap measurement and in both full project runs, and all six recorded CI failures of this row were the Conversation assertion, so no evidence puts a flake there.
